# Adjacent and Alternative Paradigms

These works are useful boundary cases or alternatives: peer co-distillation, self/EMA distillation, privileged views, sibling rollouts, and offline replay. Their evidence notes state exactly which strict-MOPD condition does not hold.

**6 records · metadata verified through 2026-08-31 · [Taxonomy](../resources/taxonomy.md)**

## Offline

<a id="arxiv-2607-19450"></a>
- [REGEN: Replay-recycling for Expert-to-Generalist distillation with Offline Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19450) - 2026-07-21. An explicit offline alternative to MOPD that recycles specialist RL replay memory and matches MOPD at lower coupled rollout-training cost.
  - **Facets:** `arxiv:2607.19450` · Method · Offline · State: Replay Buffer
  - **Teacher topology:** Specialist Pool, Independent Multi-Teacher
  - **Mechanism:** Direct Matching · Secondary: Routing and Selection
  - **Signals and domains:** Teacher-Generated Data, Action Distribution, Feedback / Reward · General LLMs
  - **Classification evidence:** REGEN recycles specialist replay memories through offline RL, making it an explicit lower-coupling alternative rather than on-policy MOPD.
  - **Artifacts:** [Code](https://github.com/yunjie-sysu/REGEN)


## On Policy

<a id="arxiv-2606-30626"></a>
- [DOPD: Dual On-policy Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30626) - 2026-06-29. Routes token supervision between privileged teacher and privileged student policies; dual-source rather than a standard pool of independent teachers.
  - **Facets:** `arxiv:2606.30626` · Method · On Policy · State: Current Student
  - **Teacher topology:** Privileged Views, Single Teacher
  - **Mechanism:** Routing and Selection · Secondary: Direct Matching, Adaptive Weighting
  - **Signals and domains:** Logits / Distribution, Sampled-Token Advantage · LLM Reasoning, Multimodal
  - **Classification evidence:** DOPD routes token supervision between one privileged external teacher and a privileged student view, not a pool of independent teachers.
  - **Artifacts:** None verified


## Online Peer

<a id="arxiv-2606-14368"></a>
- [Be My Tutor: On-Policy Co-Distillation for Mutual LLM Improvement via Peer Feedback](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14368) - 2026-06-12. Two domain-specialized peers tutor each other through feedback-conditioned self-distillation loops to achieve mutual Pareto improvement.
  - **Facets:** `arxiv:2606.14368` · Method · Online Peer · State: Current Student
  - **Teacher topology:** Peer Mutual
  - **Mechanism:** Collective Deliberation · Secondary: Direct Matching, Adaptive Weighting
  - **Signals and domains:** Responses / Rationales, Feedback / Reward · General LLMs
  - **Classification evidence:** Two trainable domain peers tutor each other bidirectionally; each learner lacks a fixed multi-teacher-to-one-student supervisor pool.
  - **Artifacts:** None verified

<a id="arxiv-2605-08873"></a>
- [CoDistill-GRPO: A Co-Distillation Recipe for Efficient Group Relative Policy Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08873) - 2026-05-09. Bidirectionally co-distills two trainable policies inside GRPO rather than consolidating a frozen multi-teacher pool.
  - **Facets:** `arxiv:2605.08873` · Method · Online Peer · State: Current Student
  - **Teacher topology:** Peer Mutual
  - **Mechanism:** Direct Matching · Secondary: Adaptive Weighting
  - **Signals and domains:** Logits / Distribution, Feedback / Reward · LLM Reasoning, LLM Alignment
  - **Classification evidence:** Two trainable policies co-distill bidirectionally inside GRPO instead of consolidating several independent teachers into one student.
  - **Artifacts:** None verified


## Self-Distillation

<a id="arxiv-2605-12652"></a>
- [Multi-Rollout On-Policy Distillation via Peer Successes and Failures](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12652) - 2026-05-12. Constructs peer-conditioned teacher signals from successful and failed sibling rollouts; multiple rollouts, not multiple independent teachers.
  - **Facets:** `arxiv:2605.12652` · Method · Self-Distillation · State: Current Student
  - **Teacher topology:** Privileged Views
  - **Mechanism:** Conflict Resolution · Secondary: Adaptive Weighting, Direct Matching
  - **Signals and domains:** Sampled-Token Advantage, Responses / Rationales, Feedback / Reward · LLM Reasoning
  - **Classification evidence:** The supervision contrasts successful and failed sibling rollouts from one policy; multi denotes rollouts rather than independent teachers.
  - **Artifacts:** None verified

<a id="arxiv-2605-06597"></a>
- [UniSD: Towards a Unified Self-Distillation Framework for Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06597) - 2026-05-07. Combines EMA teachers, multi-teacher agreement, contrastive alignment, and clipping in a self-distillation framework.
  - **Facets:** `arxiv:2605.06597` · Method · Self-Distillation · State: Near-Current Student
  - **Teacher topology:** Self / EMA, Privileged Views
  - **Mechanism:** Conflict Resolution · Secondary: Adaptive Weighting, Direct Matching
  - **Signals and domains:** Logits / Distribution, Features · General LLMs
  - **Classification evidence:** EMA/self teachers and agreement views come from one student lineage, so the framework is self-distillation rather than independent multi-teacher OPD.
  - **Artifacts:** [Code](https://github.com/Ahren09/UniSD)
